principles: Single trust root: the whole subsystem digests through ONE canonicalizer, so CANON is a leaf module importing only node:crypto.
Fail closed at config load: an unsafe or under-specified policy refuses to resolve rather than silently clamping to a safe-looking value.
Prove, don't assert: 'no existing canonicalizer can serve' is demonstrated by a committed differential test, not by prose a later reviewer must trust.
Diagnostic-only: this story reports (doctor line) but never gates; enforcement and runtime execution are other stories.
Honest scope: no string claims tamper-resistance beyond the §0.6 assurance tier.
drivers: CANON correctness is load-bearing: a wrong key order or dropped null forks digests across hosts and silently corrupts every downstream W2 record.
The 14-key policySnapshot digest must be reproducible bit-for-bit by two implementations, so defaults are pinned to a frozen literal and unknown keys reject.
pinnedPath is host-specific and required-with-no-default, so the config must NOT ship a redEvidence block yet the doctor consumer must still render a live line.

options.name: New RFC 8785 leaf (canon.ts)
pros: Correct UTF-16 code-unit key order, preserved JSON null, minimal number encoding (= JSON.stringify) verified equivalent
Single import (node:crypto), reusable by every W2 story
Differentially provable against the two existing helpers
cons: Must pin frozen digest vectors and prove the differential once

options.name: Reuse core/digest.ts digestCanonicalJson
cons: Sorts keys by a.localeCompare(b) (locale-dependent) not UTF-16 code unit, giving host/locale-forking order for keys like {B,a}

options.name: Reuse core/authority-signing.ts canonicalJsonForSigning
cons: Maps JSON null to undefined and DROPS it, so a chain-founding priorRecordDigest:null field vanishes and forks the record digest
code-POINT not code-UNIT order (differs for astral chars)
String() fallback for unknown types, not RFC 8785

rationale: CANON is the subsystem's single digest trust root; both existing helpers are provably wrong for it (digest.ts uses localeCompare key order, authority-signing drops JSON null), and either reuse would silently fork digests across hosts. A ~20-line leaf whose RFC 8785 output equals code-unit-sorted rebuild + preserved null + JSON.stringify (empirically verified: number/escape encoding and default .sort() already match RFC 8785) is both correct and cheap, and the committed differential test freezes that correctness so no later reviewer re-litigates it.

preMortem.scenario: Fudged policy default returns a plausible-but-wrong snapshot
preMortem.trigger: Implementer abbreviates the 1..255 exit-code array or mis-transcribes a default cwd/adapter
preMortem.consequence: The resolver silently yields a non-spec policySnapshot that later stories digest and trust
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke asserts policyDigest equals an independently-pinned frozen sha256 literal built from the spec's exact defaults, so any deviation flips the digest and fails RED-then-GREEN

preMortem.trigger: The health check throws or returns non-zero when the policy is missing/invalid
preMortem.consequence: lattice doctor changes exit code and a diagnostic-only feature becomes a gate
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-008 proves doctor's exit code and proofstory_gate_check output stay byte-identical; the line is pure report

preMortem.trigger: Developer reads the rule backward (rejects non-tracked, permits tracked-material globs)
preMortem.consequence: Legitimate excludes like node_modules/** are blocked while a glob hiding tracked material code is allowed
preMortem.mitigation: Fail-closed matrix asserts node_modules/** is KEPT while a glob matching a tracked material path and a bare ** are REJECTED

preMortem.scenario: A §1.12 floor is silently clamped instead of rejected
preMortem.trigger: minMatcherLen 3 quietly raised to 4 rather than failing config load
preMortem.consequence: An anti-fabrication floor is bypassed and the snapshot merely records the bypass
preMortem.mitigation: Matrix asserts the exact named diagnostic is emitted and NO clamped snapshot is produced

preMortem.scenario: CANON number/string edge cases diverge from RFC 8785
preMortem.trigger: -0, 1e21, control chars, or astral-plane keys encoded differently than RFC 8785
preMortem.mitigation: Frozen CANON vectors cover each edge case; verified up front that JSON.stringify already emits RFC-8785 minimal forms and default .sort() gives code-unit order
